arxiv-1506-05400.title: Detailed description of exclusive muon capture rates using realistic two-body forces
arxiv-1506-05400.creator: P.G. Giannaka, T.S Kosmas
arxiv-1506-05400.description: Abstract Starting from state-by-state calculations of exclusive rates of the ordinary muon capture (OMC), we evaluated total μ − \mu^{-} -capture rates for a set of light- and medium-weight nuclear isotopes. We employed a version of the proton-neutron quasi-particle random phase approximation (pn-QRPA, for short) which uses as realistic nuclear forces the Bonn C-D one boson exchange potential.

arxiv-2203-13325.title: The inverse scattering transform for weak Wigner-von Neumann type potentials Thanks: The first author is supported by CONACYT grant 61517/2020. Thanks: The second author is supported in part by the NSF under grant DMS 1716975.
arxiv-2203-13325.creator: Sergei Grudsky, Alexei Rybkin
arxiv-2203-13325.description: Abstract . In the context of the Cauchy problem for the Korteweg-de Vries equation we extend the inverse scattering transform to initial data that behave at plus infinity like a sum of Wigner-von Neumann type potentials with small coupling constants. Our arguments are based on the theory of Hankel operators. 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification 34B20, 37K15, 47B35 1.

arxiv-2205-00077.title: Who’s the Expert? On Multi-source Belief Change
arxiv-2205-00077.creator: Joseph Singleton, Richard Booth
arxiv-2205-00077.description: Abstract Consider the following belief change/merging scenario. A group of information sources gives a sequence of reports about the state of the world at various instances (e.g. different points in time). The true states at these instances are unknown to us.

arxiv-2210-08804.title: A GPU-specialized Inference Parameter Server for Large-Scale Deep Recommendation Models Volume: 0 0 0 0 Conference: Sixteenth ACM Conference on Recommender Systems; September 18–23, 2022; Seattle, WA, USA Sixteenth ACM Conference on Recommender Systems (RecSys ’22), September 18–23, 2022, Seattle, W
arxiv-2210-08804.creator: Yingcan Wei, Matthias Langer, Fan Yu, Minseok Lee, Kingsley Liu, Jerry Shi, Joey Wang
arxiv-2210-08804.description: Abstract . Recommendation systems are of crucial importance for a variety of modern apps and web services, such as news feeds, social networks, e-commerce, search, etc . To achieve peak prediction accuracy, modern recommendation models combine deep learning with terabyte-scale embedding tables to obtain a fine-grained representation of the underlying data.

arxiv-2310-19933.title: Derivation and travelling wave analysis of phenotype-structured haptotaxis models of cancer invasion
arxiv-2310-19933.creator: Tommaso Lorenzi, Fiona R Macfarlane, Kevin J Painter
arxiv-2310-19933.description: Abstract We formulate haptotaxis models of cancer invasion wherein the infiltrating cancer cells can occupy a spectrum of states in phenotype space, ranging from ‘fully mesenchymal’ to ‘fully epithelial’. The more mesenchymal cells are those that display stronger haptotaxis responses and have greater capacity to modify the extracellular matrix (ECM) through enhanced secretion of matrix-degrading enzymes (MDEs).

arxiv-2403-02930.title: A Second Look on BASS – Boosting Abstractive Summarization with Unified Semantic Graphs
arxiv-2403-02930.creator: Osman Alperen Koraş and Jörg Schlötterer and Christin Seifert
arxiv-2403-02930.description: Abstract We present a detailed replication study of the BASS framework, an abstractive summarization system based on the notion of Unified Semantic Graphs. Our investigation includes challenges in replicating key components and an ablation study to systematically isolate error sources rooted in replicating novel components. Our findings reveal discrepancies in performance compared to the original work.

arxiv-2412-07368.title: Critical velocity for wake vortex generation behind a plate in a superflow
arxiv-2412-07368.creator: Haruya Kokubo 1 , Hiromitsu Takeuchi 2,3 and Kenichi Kasamatsu 1
arxiv-2412-07368.description: Abstract We study theoretically the critical velocity U c U_{c} for quantum vortex generation by a thin plate-shaped obstacle moving through a uniform Bose-Einstein condensate. Our results based on the Gross-Pitaevskii theory reveal that the critical velocity monotonically decreases with increasing plate size L L .

arxiv-2508-08303.title: Evaluation of an Autonomous Surface Robot Equipped with a Transformable Mobility Mechanism for Efficient Mobility Control
arxiv-2508-08303.creator: Yasuyuki Fujii, Dinh Tuan Tran and Joo-Ho Lee
arxiv-2508-08303.description: Abstract . Efficient mobility and power consumption are critical for autonomous water surface robots in long-term water environmental monitoring. This study develops and evaluates a transformable mobility mechanism for a water surface robot with two control modes: station-keeping and traveling to improve energy efficiency and maneuverability.

arxiv-2509-15670.title: Effect of correlation on the elastic scattering of slow positrons from molecules.
arxiv-2509-15670.creator: Snigdha Sharma, Dhanoj Gupta
arxiv-2509-15670.description: Abstract Many-body correlation plays a crucial role in the low-energy positron-molecule scattering dynamics. In the present work, we have integrated a recent model correlation potential, developed by Swann and Gribakin, with the single-center expansion method and verified its efficacy in reproducing the best of ab initio and experimental results, for both non-polar and polar molecules.

arxiv-2512-21475.title: Physics-informed Diffusion Models for Multi-scale Prediction of Reference Signal Received Power in Wireless Networks Thanks: X. Qi, Y. Wang, Z. Wang, and Y. Li are with the Department of Electronic Engineering, BNRist, Tsinghua University, Beijing 100084, China. Thanks: H. Chai is with the State Key
arxiv-2512-21475.creator: Xiaoqian Qi, Haoye Chai 1, Yue Wang, Zhaocheng Wang
arxiv-2512-21475.description: Abstract The Reference Signal Received Power (RSRP) is a crucial factor that determines communication performance in mobile networks. Accurately predicting the RSRP can help network operators perceive user experiences and maximize throughput by optimizing wireless resources. However, existing research into RSRP prediction has limitations in accuracy and verisimilitude.

britannica-1911-moody-dwight-lyman.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-moody-dwight-lyman.description: Article 'Moody, Dwight Lyman' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 18), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. (Northfield township), Massachusetts, on the 5th of February 1837. His father died in 1841, and young Dwight, a mischievous independent boy, got a scanty schooling. In 1854 he became a salesman in a shoe-store in Boston; in 1855 he was “converted”; and in 1856 he went to Chicago and started business there.

pmc-10782925.title: Drug–drug interaction prediction: databases, web servers and computational models
pmc-10782925.creator: Yan Zhao, Jun Yin, Li Zhang, Yong Zhang, Xing Chen
pmc-10782925.description: In clinical treatment, two or more drugs (i.e. drug combination) are simultaneously or successively used for therapy with the purpose of primarily enhancing the therapeutic efficacy or reducing drug side effects. However, inappropriate drug combination may not only fail to improve efficacy, but even lead to adverse reactions.

pmc-11442860.title: Association of sedentary behavior and physical activity with occurrence of signs and symptoms in participants of a cardiac rehabilitation program
pmc-11442860.creator: João Pedro Lucas Neves Silva, Felipe Ribeiro, Heloisa Balotari Valente, Lais Manata Vanzella, Maria Julia Lopez Laurino, Guilherme da Silva Soares do Nascimento, Alice Haniuda Moliterno, William Rodrigues Tebar, Diego Giulliano Destro Christofaro, Luiz Carlos Marques Vanderlei
pmc-11442860.description: Sedentary behavior (SB) is associated with health impairments, while physical activity (PA) has been a protective factor. It is unclear whether SB and PA are associated with occurrence of signs and/or symptoms (SS) during cardiac rehabilitation program (CRP) exercise sessions. The objective was to evaluate the association between SB and PA with occurrence of SS.

pmc-11599979.title: Defining critical quality attributes and composition parameters for burn wound dressings: Antibiotic-anesthetic films as a model
pmc-11599979.creator: María Florencia Sanchez, Laura Carolina Luciani-Giacobbe, Fiamma Barbieri, María Eugenia Olivera
pmc-11599979.description: The management of wounds primarily revolves around pain relief, effective infection control and the promotion of tissue regeneration to prevent complications like chronic skin wounds. While polymeric bioactive films are innovative alternatives to conventional wound dressings, there exists a dearth of guidance regarding their quality control.

pmc-11622705.title: Traumatic multiple-level continuous and noncontinuous thoracolumbar spinal fractures management in adult patients: A single-center experience
pmc-11622705.creator: Çağlar Türk, Nail Ozdemir
pmc-11622705.description: BACKGROUND:This study aimed to describe our clinical experience with surgical approaches and patient management for traumatic multiple-level continuous and noncontinuous thoracolumbar spinal fractures.METHODS:We retrospectively evaluated patients with continuous and noncontinuous multiple-level thoracolumbar fractures who were operated on by the same surgical team from 2019 to 2021.

pmc-12500839.title: Saireito (TJ-114) for Preventing High-Output Syndrome After Temporary Ileostomy in Rectal Cancer Surgery
pmc-12500839.creator: Mamoru Uemura, Chikako Kusunoki, Yuki Sekido, Mitsunobu Takeda, Tsuyoshi Hata, Atsushi Hamabe, Takayuki Ogino, Norikatsu Miyoshi, Mitsuyoshi Tei, Yoshinori Kagawa, Hidetoshi Eguchi, Yuichiro Doki
pmc-12500839.description: PurposeIn rectal cancer surgery, a temporary ileostomy is often created to prevent clinical anastomotic leakage. However, high-output syndrome (HOS) frequently arises as a postoperative complication. We aimed to investigate the preventive effect of Saireito, a traditional Japanese herbal medicine, on HOS in patients with a temporary ileostomy.

pmc-12524305.title: The Impact of Social Determinants of Health on Supportive and Palliative Care in Pancreatic Cancer Management: A Narrative Review
pmc-12524305.creator: Sterre van Herwijnen, Vishnu Jayaprakash, Camila Hidalgo Salinas, Joseph R Habib, Daniel Brock Hewitt, Greg D Sacks, Christopher L Wolfgang, Katherine A Morgan, Brian J Kaplan, Michael D Kluger, Alok Aggarwal, Ammar A Javed, Eduardo Bruera
pmc-12524305.description: Simple SummaryPancreatic cancer is one of the deadliest solid organ malignancies, with a 5-year survival rate of 13% across all stages of disease. Supportive and palliative care are critical aspects of patient management and can be impacted by social determinants of health (SDOH), such as income, education, and access to healthcare.

pmc-12979174.title: TGF-β in hematologic malignancies: molecular functions and clinical applications
pmc-12979174.creator: Ruiyang Li, Fang Wei, Mengbo Yang
pmc-12979174.description: Transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) represents a family of multifunctional cytokines, primarily secreted by megakaryocytes, monocytes, T lymphocytes, bone marrow stromal cells, and other cell types. TGF-β plays an essential role in various physiological processes, including the regulation of cell proliferation, differentiation, apoptosis, and immune homeostasis.

pmc-13351485.title: Energy Transfer in Nanodroplet‐Based Luminescent Solar Concentrators
pmc-13351485.creator: Lorenzo Vallan, Julia W. Mikurenda, Alex Parra Sánchez‐Camacho, Maria Lili, Sebastian J. M. Robben, Stefan C. J. Meskers, Michael G. Debije, Claudio Roscini
pmc-13351485.description: Luminescent solar concentrators are promising devices for building‐integrated photovoltaics, but their efficiency is limited by aggregation‐induced quenching at high fluorophore concentrations and reabsorption losses during lightguide propagation. Here, we present a nanoconfinement strategy that addresses these challenges by embedding organic dyes within oil nanodroplets dispersed in polyvinyl alcohol coatings.

pmc-13448187.title: Stochasticity dominated adaptive assembly of benthic microbiota across oasis-to-desert sections of an arid inland river
pmc-13448187.creator: Yongcheng Chen, Yingchao Sun, Rongzheng Huang, Shuangming Li, Yuhang Liu, Xingke Yuan, Xinyi Chen, Junfeng Li, Lihe Yin, Chunhui Ma, Fanfan Zhang
pmc-13448187.description: SummarySediment microbial communities in arid inland rivers are important for biogeochemical cycling, but the assembly mechanisms and network responses across the transition from irrigated oases to desert margins remain unclear. We investigated bacterial and fungal communities in Yarkand River sediments along salinity and nutrient gradients using 16S rRNA and ITS sequencing, sediment chemistry, iCAMP null-model analysis, and co-occurrence networks.

pmc-13543093.title: Sleep fragmentation and heightened inflammation: A latent profile subtype predicting nine-year major depressive disorder severity in the MIDUS study
pmc-13543093.creator: Nur Hani Zainal, Sherry A Beaudreau
pmc-13543093.description: BackgroundCross-sectional and standard approaches to examining proinflammatory activity and sleep disturbances separately hinder understanding of their additive, long-term impacts on major depressive disorder (MDD). The current study used latent profile analysis (LPA) to identify multimodal neuroimmune profiles and to investigate whether subtypes predicted 9-year MDD severity in a community-dwelling adult sample.

pmc-13604916.title: Dynamic Contrast-Enhanced MRI in Neuro-Oncology: A Narrative and Translational Review
pmc-13604916.creator: Francesca Bozzetti, Ana Ramos-González, Alessandro Leonetti, Chiara Tommasi, Marcello Tiseo, Francesco Salaroli, Giovanni Ceccon, Ilaria Renna, Marco Galaverni, Nicola Sverzellati, Daniele Corbo
pmc-13604916.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background/Objectives: Dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI) is emerging as a key technique in neuro-oncologic imaging by enabling quantitative assessment of vascular permeability and blood–brain barrier integrity, two central features of tumor progression and treatment-related tissue injury. Its clinical relevance is particularly evident in the post-treatment setting, where conventional MRI lacks specificity and entities such as tumor progression, pseudoprogression, and radiation necrosis frequently overlap.

pmc-13675970.title: Dose-dependent cardiac autonomic dysregulation under classroom crowding: heart rate variability analysis and machine learning classification
pmc-13675970.creator: Mohamed Naeem
pmc-13675970.description: Classroom overcrowding affects hundreds of millions of students globally, yet its physiological impact on cardiac autonomic function remains uncharacterized. This controlled within-subjects experiment enrolled 30 healthy university students who attended standardized 30-min lectures under three calibrated density conditions: low (30 students/150 m2), medium (60/150 m2), and high (100/150 m2), with all environmental parameters held constant.
